filters()

The filters() method registers pure filter functions on a FeatureCell that execute during the Filter stage of the pipeline. Filters refine or suppress candidate state values before reduction while preserving the structural shape of state.

Method Contract Summary

  • Filter functions are registered declaratively on a FeatureCell instance
  • Filters execute before reducers and taps
  • Filters receive the candidate next value
  • Filters must be pure and side-effect free
  • Errors propagate as Vault errors

The filters() method defines value refinement only. It does not mutate existing state, does not emit snapshots, and does not influence pipeline scheduling or control flow. Its responsibility is limited to accepting, refining, or suppressing candidate values prior to reduction. For details on how referential isolation is enforced at every stage boundary, see Pipeline Isolation.

The filters() method is additive. It may be invoked multiple times, and each invocation appends filter functions to the FeatureCell’s filter list. Filters execute in the exact order they are registered during initialization.

While multiple invocations are supported, the recommended practice is to register related filters as a single ordered array to preserve clarity and intentional execution ordering.

Registers pure filter functions that execute during the Filter stage. Filters refine or suppress candidate values while preserving structural type and do not mutate state or influence pipeline control flow.
Example

The filters() method registers one or more filter functions that evaluate candidate next values during pipeline execution. Each filter may refine the value, return it unchanged, or suppress the update by returning undefined.

What this does

  • Registers one or more filter functions on the FeatureCell
  • Filters execute before reducers
  • Filters receive the candidate next value
  • Returning undefined suppresses snapshot emission

This demonstrates the intended use of filters() as a declarative mechanism for value acceptance, refinement, or rejection prior to reduction.

Example: Registering Filter Functions

{{`
@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {

  private readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault
      .filters(
        [
          (employees) => employees.filter(e => e.active)
        ]
      ).initialize();
  }
}
`}}
 
{{`
export const employeeCell = FeatureCell({
  key: 'employees',
  initialState: [{ name: 'John', age: 30 }] 
});

employeeCell
  .filters(
    [
      (employees) => employees.filter(e => e.active)
    ]
  ).initialize();
`}}
